articles.title: IND vs NZ: After sitting out four games, Mohammed Siraj gets his chance in fifth ODI; Yash Thakur makes debut
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj finally got an opportunity in the series as India brought back the experienced pacer for the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand at Bay
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj finally got an opportunity in the series as India brought back the experienced pacer for the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. It is Siraj's first appearance in the series. He last played an ODI against the West Indies in October."Siraj has been craving an opportunity to play in all formats. He's been around the team for a while and is pretty experienced. He's played over the years, so he knows how to go about things. We're super excited for him as well," India captain Shreyas Iyer said at the toss.New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and elected to bowl in the series-deciding match. India lead the five-match series 2-1 after winning the first two games, while the third ODI was washed out. The visitors, however, suffered a 244-run defeat in the fourth match on Friday.India also handed a debut to right-arm seamer Yash Thakur. "He's a jovial guy who has been waiting for the opportunity to play for the country and has been in the scheme of things for a while. I'm glad he's getting the opportunity to prove himself today. It's his debut, so good luck to him," Iyer said.India's Gurnoor Brar and New Zealand's Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson will miss the final ODI as they prepare for the two-Test series, which begins on November 19.Teams:India: Rohit Sharma, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (c), Ishan Kishan (wk), Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Arshdeep Singh, Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur.New Zealand: Tim Seifert (wk), Will Young, Nick Kelly, Dean Foxcroft, Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Kristian Clarke, Blair Tickner, Jacob Duffy, Matthew FisherGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaryavir, a Rishabh Pant fan, learnt to refrain from copying father Sehwag
articles.summary: When Virender Sehwag dropped his 11-year-old son Aaryavir at the Sonnet Cricket Club eight years ago, he made just one request to the coaches, the late
articles.body: When Virender Sehwag dropped his 11-year-old son Aaryavir at the Sonnet Cricket Club eight years ago, he made just one request to the coaches, the late Tarak Sinha and Devender Sharma. “Don’t hesitate to be strict with him. He is just another kid learning cricket here. That's all he told us,” Devender told TOI.“Viru barely called us to enquire about how his sons were coached. He must have talked to them personally but never interfered in our job. The only time he made a call about Aaryavir’s cricket was during the Covid lockdown. He shot some videos of some of his batting drills and sent them to us to check,” he added.Aaryavir was given a swanky car to come to the ground, but the chauffer was strictly instructed against carrying his kit bags. Be it the cricket gear or the food he ate there, nothing was special. His demeanour didn’t give him away as the son of one of India’s greatest match-winners.Now, over the last 10 days in Al Amerat in Oman, Aaryavir has taken significant steps towards developing his own identity. His ended as the player of the tournament, scoring 361 runs.Like his father did in his first big final against England at Lord’s in 2002, Aaryavir set up India’s big chase at the top of the order on Saturday with 58 off 61 balls. “Since I got out in the last match against them (Pakistan), I wanted to score today, regardless of copping a blow on my arm. I knew if I stayed in the middle, it would keep building the pressure on Pakistan,” Aaryavir words after the final were reminiscent of Sehwag's unfettered ways.It’s worth noticing that Aaryavir’s runs have not come in the same menacing way that the senior Sehwag was known for. “He has learnt to refrain from copying Viru,” Devender, who has played U-19 and first-class cricket with Sehwag, told TOI. Instead, Aaryavir used to be in awe of Rishabh Pant. “He used to go home and keep talking about Rishabh. Whenever Rishabh came for practice, he would intently watch him,” Devender said."There is some obvious reflection of Viru's talent in him. One must understand Viru was a freak and a beast. But Aaryavir is a very cerebral cricketer. When he first came, he compulsively tried to smack every ball off the front foot because he may have seen highlights of his father's batting," said Devender. "But, he likes to have deep discussions on cricket and tried to understand why he was getting out quickly. He realised the importance of being a good off the back foot and playing square of the wicket just like his father did. I am pleased that he scored a 160 in this tournament because he has been working hard on cracking the code to construct big innings," he added.Devender emphasizes on Viru's lack of interference in how both his sons are raised in the cricket field and helped them develop their individuality. Sehwag's uncluttered mind helped him revel as a player. Aaryavir may have done his bit in shedding some of the burden of carrying his father's name. It's time to build on it!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma miss the beat in their last dance on New Zealand soil
articles.summary: MIUNT MANGANUI: The coastal city of Tauranga broke away from the wet script witnessed in Auckland, Wellington and Hamilton, but even the bright sunshine
articles.body: MIUNT MANGANUI: The coastal city of Tauranga broke away from the wet script witnessed in Auckland, Wellington and Hamilton, but even the bright sunshine couldn't change the narrative for Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli in New Zealand. The experienced campaigners managed series hauls of just 86 and 30 runs, respectively, in conditions that remained challenging for batters.The ODI specialists would have liked better returns, but their last dance in New Zealand never found the right beat. Kohli did score an authoritative 74 in the series opener at Eden Park but lost rhythm after that. His last three scores were 7, 0 and 5. For Rohit, it was a difficult tour, with two ducks, and he crossed the double-digit mark only once. On only their second overseas tour of the year, the two right-handers struggled against pace, bounce, movement and the sheer relentlessness of the Kiwi quicks.Their vulnerabilities against the moving ball were exposed as the opposition didn't give an inch, persisting with the good-length spot and coupling it with movement in either direction. Both were caught on the crease in the fourth ODI and lacked confidence in the final fixture. Rohit mistimed a flick, while Kohli slashed at a delivery outside off, leaving India in trouble in both fixtures even before the spectators could settle down.While Matt Henry operated in unplayable territory on Friday, Sunday afternoon was a perfect occasion to cash in. More than movement off the pitch or in the air, it was their shot selection that kept the two batters' series hauls low. Overall, 2026 has been a rewarding year for the two, but New Zealand has been an opposition against which Rohit hasn't enjoyed any success, both at home and away. As far as Kohli is concerned, it was a rare failure after what has been a very high-scoring year for India's No. 3.Misfiring top orderIndia's top order misfired throughout the series, and this was the first occasion in over five years when none of the top three scored an individual hundred. It has happened only twice since the 2013 Champions Trophy that India's top order failed to reach the three-figure mark in a five-match series. Interestingly, both instances came against the same opposition: New Zealand, in 2019 and now during this tour.This away vulnerability will definitely serve as a stern wake-up call in the build-up to the 2027 ODI World Cup, where head coach Gautam Gambhir expects similar conditions. India will again find home comfort against Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe after this tour, but doubts over whether the batting has what it takes to dominate in South Africa will continue.For the first time in over 10 years, Kohli registered three single-digit scores in an ODI series, while the two ducks saw Rohit join several unwanted lists. There are no doubts about their abilities in the format, but it now remains to be seen how the think tank reviews these struggles as it firms up its plans for next year's multi-nation event.India will need experience in South Africa, but more than that, they will need two firing and assured batters in the top three.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli hits 11-year low as India suffer another batting collapse in New Zealand
articles.summary: Virat Kohli endured a difficult ODI series against New Zealand, managing just 86 runs in four innings as India suffered another batting collapse in the
articles.body: Virat Kohli endured a difficult ODI series against New Zealand, managing just 86 runs in four innings as India suffered another batting collapse in the fifth and final match in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. The 38-year-old had arrived in New Zealand after scoring runs in India's previous ODI series against the West Indies, but could not carry that form into the contest against the Black Caps.Kohli, who holds the record for the most ODI runs against New Zealand, started the series with a 74 off 51 balls in the opening match at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4. However, his scores in the next three innings were 7, 0 and 5, respectively.The three single-digit scores in the second, fourth and fifth ODIs marked a first for Kohli in 11 years. The right-handed batter had last recorded three single-digit scores in an ODI series in 2015.Since making his ODI debut against Sri Lanka in Dambulla on August 18, 2008, Kohli had previously registered three single-digit scores in a bilateral series against Pakistan during their tour of India in December 2012-January 2013. He scored 0, 6 and 7 in the matches played in Chennai, Kolkata and Delhi, respectively.Kohli has also had two other ODI tournaments in which he recorded three single-digit scores. These came during the 2011 World Cup and the Carlton Mid ODI Tri-Series in Australia in 2014-15.Kohli's three single-digit scores in an ODI series or tournament:- 2011 World Cup- Pakistan in India, 2012-13- Carlton Mid ODI Tri-Series, Australia, 2014-15- India vs New Zealand, 2026India's batting struggles continued in the fifth ODI, with New Zealand bowling out the visitors for 209 in the series decider in Mount Maunganui on Sunday. The hosts' bowlers maintained their lines and troubled the Indian batters, putting themselves in a position to level the series.The Shreyas Iyer-led side had been expected to put up a better performance after being bowled out for 89 at the same venue in the fourth ODI a couple of days earlier. However, India suffered another batting collapse despite entering the final match with a 2-1 lead in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Arshdeep Singh equals two batting records with quickfire knock in fifth ODI
articles.summary: Arshdeep Singh made the most of his brief stay at the crease after walking out to bat at No.
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh made the most of his brief stay at the crease after walking out to bat at No. 11 for India in the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand on Sunday. The left-arm pacer scored 14 runs off just four balls, hitting two sixes before being dismissed by Jacob Duffy in the 43rd over.Arshdeep opened his account with a six off the first ball he faced, sending Duffy over the boundary. He hit another six off the third delivery before Duffy dismissed him on the first ball of the 43rd over.The two sixes helped Arshdeep match two batting records for India in ODIs. By hitting a six off the first ball of his innings, he became only the third Indian No. 11 batter to achieve the feat.Before Arshdeep, Venkatesh Prasad and Jasprit Bumrah had also hit sixes off the first ball of their innings while batting at No. 11 for India.Prasad achieved the feat against Australia in the quarter-final of the 2000 Champions Trophy, then known as the ICC Knockout Trophy, in Nairobi. Bumrah hit Pat Cummins for a six off the first ball of his innings in an ODI against Australia in Mohali on March 10, 2019.India No. 11 batters to hit a six off the first ball of their innings in an ODI:- Venkatesh Prasad off Ian Harvey (Australia), Nairobi, 2000 Champions Trophy quarter-final- Jasprit Bumrah off Pat Cummins (Australia), Mohali, 2019- Arshdeep Singh off Jacob Duffy (New Zealand), Mount Maunganui, 2026Where data is availableArshdeep's two sixes also helped him equal the record for the most sixes by an Indian No. 11 batter in an ODI innings. Venkatesh Prasad and Mohammed Shami had previously hit two sixes each in an innings while batting at No. 11.Most sixes by an Indian No. 11 batter in an ODI innings:- 2 – Venkatesh Prasad vs Pakistan, Toronto, 1996- 2 – Mohammed Shami vs Sri Lanka, Fatullah, 2014- 2 – Arshdeep Singh vs New Zealand, Mount Maunganui, 2026Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Everyone knew': Ex-Australia bowler Chadd Sayers fires fresh salvo at Pat Cummins over sandpaper scandal
articles.summary: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the
articles.body: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has challenged Pat Cummins’ version of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper during the South Africa tour.Sayers, who was part of the touring squad, said he believed every player was aware of what was happening. He also disagreed with Cummins’ statement that there was no team discussion about taking collective responsibility after the incident.“I’m comfortable sitting here … that I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used,” Sayers told SEN radio on Sunday. “I’m not taking sides. I’m neutral in all this, I’m just trying to tell my side of the story and what I believe happened.”The controversy has returned to the spotlight following Khawaja’s autobiography, in which he claimed the entire team knew about the sandpaper plan and suggested Australia had used ball-tampering methods even before the Cape Town Test in 2018.Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s allegations as “complete nonsense” during a press conference on Friday. However, Sayers was unhappy with how the Australian captain addressed the issue, particularly his personal comments about Khawaja.“I didn’t like how he [Cummins] did go at Usman and got personal. I probably get why but I don’t think it needed to happen.”Sayers recalls team meeting after scandalSayers also remembered a lengthy discussion among players after the incident came to light. This contradicts Cummins’ version of events.“We all sat in the change rooms after that day’s play, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, and just talked about what had happened and where to next,” Sayers said.He added that he was relieved the matter was finally being discussed openly after years of players having to remain silent.Warner questions Cricket Australia's investigationMeanwhile, former vice-captain David Warner has again questioned Cricket Australia’s investigation, alleging that important information was withheld from him. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, was punished following the scandal.Warner claimed he was never informed that bowlers had been interviewed during the investigation and questioned why the governing body had not shared all the evidence with him before he accepted his punishment.“Just to clarify ‘As far as I am aware’ was the POINT,” he wrote on Instagram. “I was never told the bowlers had been interviewed or provided statements.“That information would’ve been pretty useful when I was forced to make decisions back in 2018. Why weren’t we given all the evidence by CA?”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sandpaper scandal: Bowler Chadd Sayers says he took sandpaper from the field and rejects Pat Cummins recount
articles.summary: Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says he helped take sandpaper from the field in the match prior to the Cape Town Test and backs Usman Khawaja's recollection over Pat Cummins'.
articles.body:
Former Australia bowler Chadd Sayers says he helped take sandpaper off the ground in the match before the infamous Cape Town Test and has backed Usman Khawaja's recollection over Pat Cummins' - saying he believes "everyone knew" about the plan to ball tamper.

Sayers, 39, was 12th man during the second Test of the 2018 series against South Africa in Gqeberha, previously known as Port Elizabeth, and backed the claim from Khawaja's book that sandpaper was also used there.

"It was given to me to take off," Sayers said on SEN Radio.

"That wasn't planned or anything. It was a wicket or drinks break after tea."

'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims

Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate

Sayers also said there was a "60 to 90-minute" meeting in the Australia dressing room after Bancroft had been caught using sandpaper in Cape Town, in which players discussed taking collective responsibility - something Khawaja claims but Cummins said he did not remember in his extraordinary news conference on Friday.

"I am comfortable sitting here that I believe everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," said Sayers, whose one Test was the final match of that series.

"It [sandpaper] was used in two Test matches and there were discussions in the changing rooms.

"I'm not taking sides, it's just my recollection of what took place.

"After the occurrence in Cape Town, we all sat in the changing rooms after that day's play and, probably for 60 to 90 minutes, we talked about what had happened and I guess where to next."

Sayers first backed Khawaja's recollections last week, saying "everything" in the former opener's book was "accurate".

In an episode which has dominated headlines in Australia and elsewhere, Khawaja said the entire Australia team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball and should have taken responsibility.

Cummins, a bowler in that squad and now Australia captain, emphatically rejected the claims by calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense".

The bowlers - Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon - have always claimed they did not know.

David Warner accused Cricket Australia of a "cover-up" on Saturday, suggesting Hazlewood, Starc and Lyon had not been interviewed as part of the governing body's investigation.

Warner, Bancroft and then captain Steve Smith served lengthy bans for their role in the scandal.

articles.title: Aaryavir Sehwag earns special two-word praise from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Aaryavir Sehwag enjoyed a memorable Under-19 Asia Cup campaign, earning recognition from fellow young sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after helping India
articles.body: Aaryavir Sehwag enjoyed a memorable Under-19 Asia Cup campaign, earning recognition from fellow young sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after helping India lift the title with a thrilling one-wicket victory over Pakistan.Sooryavanshi congratulated the son of former India opener Virender Sehwag through an Instagram story, sharing the tournament's leading run-scorers list with a simple message: "Star boiiiiii @aaryavirsehwag".The gesture was particularly interesting because Sooryavanshi, despite being just 15, has already established himself as one of India's most exciting young batting talents. His message was a nod to another youngster making waves in Indian cricket.Aaryavir thoroughly deserved the praise after finishing the tournament as its leading run-scorer. He collected 361 runs in five innings at an impressive average of 90.25, including one century and three half-centuries. His highest score was a magnificent 160 against the UAE.He was subsequently named Player of the Tournament.The youngster also delivered when it mattered most, scoring 58 off 61 balls against Pakistan in the final. His innings included nine boundaries and helped India build a strong foundation during their chase of 338. He shared a 95-run opening partnership with captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80.Aaryavir also caught attention with his celebration after reaching his half-century, recreating Virat Kohli's famous 'bat does the talking' gesture. Despite taking a blow to his forearm and requiring medical attention, he continued batting and contributed significantly.Mohit Ulva seals dramatic India victoryThe final turned into a thrilling contest after Pakistan posted 337/9, powered by Usman Khan's 107. India found themselves struggling at 252/8 before Manal Chauhan (47 off 32) and Mohit Ulva (49 not out off 26) staged a remarkable recovery.With three runs required from the final delivery, Ulva smashed a boundary to secure a one-wicket victory and India's ninth Under-19 Asia Cup title.For Aaryavir, the tournament was a major breakthrough, while Sooryavanshi's congratulatory message added another memorable moment to his celebrations.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England Lions: Rehan Ahmed hits hundred and takes five-for in 80-run win over West Indies A
articles.summary: Rehan Ahmed (108 off 100 balls) struck 11 fours and five sixes at No 3, before claiming 5-60 with his leg spin in the 80-run win; the Lions have won all seven of their matches on tour so far, following a 3-0 sweep in the T20 series by leading 4-0 in the five-match ODI leg
articles.body:
Rehan (108 off 100 balls) struck 11 fours and five sixes at No 3 as the Lions - who had already clinched the series, leading 3-0 - posted 330 after winning the toss in St Kitts.

The all-rounder then claimed 5-60 with his leg spin as the tourists bowled their opponents out for 250 overs in reply.

The 22-year-old has played five Test matches, 11 ODIs and 14 T20s for England since making his debut as an 18-year-old in 2022.

James Rew (51) and Jack Haynes (57) also cracked fifties during the Lions innings, the former sharing in a 137-run partnership with Rehan for the fourth wicket.

Keacy Carty (51) and Jyd Goolie (51) both hit half centuries for West Indies A but they, as well as Alick Athanaze (41), failed to kick on from encouraging starts as the hosts slipped to another defeat.

The Lions will look to clinch a 5-0 series sweep - to go with winning the T20s 3-0 - with another victory in their final ODI of the tour on Monday.

articles.title: WPL 2027: BCCI shifts Mumbai leg from Brabourne to Wankhede on ICC request; here's why
articles.summary: The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on
articles.body: The Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 will be held at the Wankhede Stadium instead of the Brabourne Stadium, the BCCI announced on Sunday. The dates and fixtures of the tournament will remain unchanged.The fifth edition of the WPL will be played from January 14 to February 7, with Vadodara and Mumbai serving as the two host cities. The first leg will take place at the BCA Stadium in Vadodara from January 14 to 24, while Mumbai will host the remaining matches from January 26 until the final on February 7.The Mumbai leg was originally scheduled to be held at the Cricket Club of India’s (CCI) Brabourne Stadium. However, the venue has been changed as CCI is also set to host the inaugural edition of the ICC Women's Champions Trophy in the T20 format, which begins on February 14. The BCCI said the gap between the two tournaments would not give the pitches enough time to recover.“The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced that the Mumbai leg of the Women’s Premier League 2027 will now be held at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, instead of the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India (CCI). The dates and fixtures will remain unchanged,” the BCCI said in a statement.“The WPL Governing Council approved the original venues and dates for the fifth edition of the TATA WPL at its meeting on 15 September 2026. Under the approved schedule, the Mumbai leg, comprising Match Nos. 12 to 20, the Eliminator and the Final, was to be played at CCI between 26 January and 7 February 2027.”“As CCI is also scheduled to host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, commencing on 14 February, the interval between the conclusion of the TATA WPL and the start of the multi-nation tournament would not provide sufficient time for the pitches to recover,” the board added.The BCCI said the venue was changed following a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC). The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg.“The change follows a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC) to shift the matches scheduled to be played at CCI. The WPL Committee has approved the change, with Wankhede Stadium now set to host all 11 matches of the Mumbai leg,” the BCCI said.The Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA), during its 95th Annual General Meeting, had formally requested the BCCI to consider it for hosting matches in case of changes to the schedules of future series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
